Because the flag is cleared on the first firing, both sides fire on turn 1 only even though the hook runs every turn. guards.what: G1 (LIVE): nothing in the sim ever sets `_pending`, so the relic does nothing in every run that buys it
guards.issue: MECHANISM: FakeVenerableTeaSet.cs:43-51 latches GainEnergyInNextCombat from AfterRoomEntered when `room is RestSiteRoom`. The sim's port implements ONLY the spend half and expects the latch as a constructor argument, `__init__(self, rested: bool = False)` (fake_venerable_tea_set.py:25-27). RunState.add_relic constructs relics through make_relic(id) with no arguments (run.py:546-548), so _pending is False for the whole run. The sim is NOT missing the pipeline the port needs: Relic.after_room_entered is a real base hook (relics/base.py:194) and run.py:982-983 dispatches it to every relic on entering EVERY room, with the room type in hand -- and the sibling relic/eternal_feather in this same batch uses exactly that hook for exactly the same RoomType.REST_SITE test. PROMPT.md bug class 12's rule applied: the premise implied by the constructor-injection design ('whether you rested is out-of-combat state, injected via the constructor') is false today. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b05.py tea-set-rest): make_relic gives _pending=False; the port has no after_room_entered override; firing the exact dispatch run.py:983 performs with RoomType.REST_SITE leaves _pending=False; and the next combat's turn-1 energy is 3 where C# gives 4. Forcing _pending=True gives 4, which proves the spend half works and isolates the defect to the missing latch. Both sides ported: the relic is bought for 50 gold from the ported Fake Merchant event (events/fake_merchant.py:18-22), rest sites are a ported room type that dispatches after_room_entered, and every act has them. The fix is one method, copied from relics/eternal_feather.py:19-22's room filter. Rule 7: relics/base.py, run.py, relics/eternal_feather.py and events/fake_merchant.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: G2 (POOL-WIDE): the same constructor-injection shape across the whole relic roster
guards.issue: This is a SHAPE, not a one-off, and it is invisible to the existing sweeps -- .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md's sweep A diffs a field across two combats, and a field that is never written looks identical on both instances, so sweep A cleared this relic. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b05.py injected-state): exactly THREE of the 258 ported relics take a constructor argument at all -- fake_venerable_tea_set(rested), venerable_tea_set(rested) and girya(times_lifted) -- and a git grep shows NOTHING under sts2_rl/ constructs any of the three with arguments. relic/venerable_tea_set is the real Tea Set (2 energy instead of 1) and has the identical defect; relic/girya's lifts come from a rest-site OPTION the relic itself appends (relics/girya.py's modify_rest_site_options), so its counter is plausibly written through that path and needs its own batch's trace rather than a verdict here. No verdict is issued for either sibling in this record -- they are reported in .superpowers/sdd/relic-batch-05-lessons.md as pre-populated work for their own batches, exactly as sweep A did for centennial_puzzle and paels_eye. Rule 7: relics/venerable_tea_set.py and relics/girya.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: N1: GainEnergyInNextCombat is a [SavedProperty] with a change-guarded setter (FakeVenerableTeaSet.cs:25-41) that flips base.Status; the sim's _pending is a plain bool
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / VfxCmd / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, the damage/heal numbers and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim. The [SavedProperty] attribute and the `if (_gainEnergyInNextCombat != value)` change guard exist for save serialization and for the relic bar's Active/Normal highlight (line 38); neither has a gameplay consequence, and the sim's relic instance persists on RunState.relics for the whole run either way, which is the persistence the flag needs.

guards.what: N2: the flag is cleared on the FIRST energy reset of the next combat, not at combat end (FakeVenerableTeaSet.cs:59)
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 13's trace: the sim also clears at the point of use (fake_venerable_tea_set.py:31), and neither side clears at a combat boundary. That is correct on both sides -- the flag has to survive from the rest site through the map to the next fight, which is precisely why a combat-boundary reset would break it. Contrast relic/belt_buckle, where the missing combat-boundary reset IS the live gap; the difference is that this flag's lifetime is deliberately longer than one combat.
